public_rationale: The February 2026 safety report describes recent improvements alongside continuing factual and logical errors [e1]. It does not measure comparable failure rates from June 2022 to June 2026 [e1]. The September 2025 finance report gives a full-year 2025 cash-burn target for OpenAI, not realized industry cash requirements through Q1 2026 [e2]. Together, these sources do not establish the trillion-dollar total, changes in comparable task costs, or the claimed changes in industry cash requirements and reliability [e1, e2].
limitations: Continuing errors do not establish unchanged reliability over four years [e1].
One company's cash-burn target does not establish a same-basis industry comparison [e2].
The packet lacks a consistently defined trillion-dollar total and matched-task cost and reliability measurements for the full period.
The claim does not define the industry perimeter or whether cash intensity means absolute spending or spending relative to output.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: After four years and a trillion dollars, AI is more expensive, AI companies are more cash-intensive, and AI products are no more reliable.

statement.excerpt: Four years and a trillion dollars in, AI is more expensive, its companies more cash-intensive, its products just as unreliable, and its boosters more desperate than ever to make you ignore reality as a means of empowering one of a few ultra-rich oafs.

our_interpretation: Assess the normalized factual proposition. The accompanying insults and claims about boosters' desperation are not measurable components.
The plain reading compares approximately June 2022 with the state of the industry at the June 2026 post.

More expensive means higher cost for comparable useful work; more cash-intensive means greater cash requirements, although the speaker does not specify absolute spending or spending relative to output.
Just as unreliable means no material improvement in failure rates on comparable tasks, not merely that errors remain possible.
For the ongoing company-finance component, the latest completed calendar quarter before the post is Q1 2026; annual disclosures can supply background but cannot automatically replace that endpoint.
The trillion-dollar amount has no stated company perimeter, accounting basis, or treatment of financing, acquisitions, spending, and future commitments.
criteria.support_condition: Consistently defined records establish approximately one trillion dollars absorbed over the stated period, increased company cash requirements, increased matched-task costs, and no material improvement in matched-task reliability.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes a material decline in task costs or improvement in reliability, or financial records contradict the spending and cash-intensity assertions under a defensible common definition. A mixed finding requires affirmative evidence for both supported and contradicted components.

evidence.locator: Section 1.2, Reliability challenges persist in current AI systems
evidence.explanation: The review documents continuing factual and reasoning failures while acknowledging improvements. It supports persistent unreliability but does not establish unchanged failure rates from 2022, and cautions against equating continuing errors with no improvement.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning OpenAI looks to meet
evidence.explanation: This is evidence of a reported OpenAI cash-burn target, not realized industry-wide cash intensity or cumulative investment. Reuters attributes it to The Information and says it could not independently verify the report; no underlying primary financial disclosure was obtained.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Consistently defined financial records covering approximately June 2022 to June 2026, with cash requirements compared through Q1 2026. These must define the industry perimeter and separate financing, realized spending and commitments without double-counting. Matched-task cost and failure-rate measurements over the claimed period would settle the cost and reliability components.
